newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Afghan group says takes two Taleban villages.
newsitem.headline: Afghan group says takes two Taleban villages.

text.p: An Afghan Shi'ite Moslem faction said on Tuesday it had taken two villages from Taleban forces in three days of fighting north of the capital Kabul as well as capturing scores of the purist Islamic movement's fighters.

"Heavy fighting has been going on for three days in Ghorband area and our forces captured Surkh and Parsa villages from the Taleban," General Mohammad Bashir Tawhidi, deputy head of the Shi'ite Hezb-i-Wahdat faction's northern council, said.

Speaking by satellite telephone from the opposition-held northern town of Mazar-i-Sharif, Tawhidi told journalists in Kabul that Wahdat forces had captured a senior Taleban commander, Mullah Abdul Wahid, with 60 fighters.
There no independent confirmation of the report and no immediate comment was available from the Taleban, which controls two-thirds of the country, including Kabul.

Tawhidi said dozens of Taleban fighters had been killed in the fighting in Ghorband valley, which is east of the Wahdat-controlled central province of Bamiyan and 160 km (100 miles) northwest of Kabul.
Taleban forces have been stalled for nearly three months below the nearby strategic Shibar pass, which can serve as passage for the Taleban to the north of the country.
Wahdat is a partner in an anti-Taleban alliance that includes forces loyal to northern Uzbek chief Abdul Rashid Dostum and ousted president Burhanuddin Rabbani.
The report of the renewed fighting in Ghorband valley follows reported attacks in eastern Afghanistan by another anti-Taleban group that was ousted from there last year.
